summary: The first episode of the Sirah Impak Sosial series sets the background before the birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Prophet Ibrahim's AS exploration of Mecca. The ustaz tells of Sarah, the Pharaoh of Egypt and the gift of Hajar, then of Hajar and the baby Ismail being left in a valley with no living thing. Hajar shows complete trust in Allah while striving between Safa and Marwah until Zamzam gushed forth. The Arab tribe of Jurhum settled, Ismail grew up as an 'Arabised Arab', and the Kaaba was rebuilt with Ibrahim's supplications in Al-Baqarah 124 to 129, including the prayer that a messenger be sent. The ustaz closes with the decline of Jurhum, the arrival of Khuza'ah and Amr ibn Luhayy, who brought the idol Hubal to Mecca, over a span of about 2,000 years before the Prophet ﷺ.
keyPoints: The Prophet ﷺ said 'I am the answer to the prayer of my father Ibrahim', so the sirah begins with Ibrahim AS, father of the exploration of Mecca, and all of us walk on his path.
Hajar showed complete trust in Allah: striving with all her might (Safa and Marwah) then leaving the rest to Allah. Effort nobody saw was raised by Allah into the rite of sa'i.
Prophet Ibrahim's prayer put his descendants' prayer and faith before provision, and the prayer that a messenger be sent from them was answered after about 2,000 years.
Two lessons from Prophet Ibrahim after building the Kaaba: humility ('accept from us') and long-term thinking about generations and the Hereafter.
Good change demands sacrifice and courage, and a calamity that brings us closer to Allah is good.
The first idol at the Kaaba was brought by Amr ibn Luhayy from Rome out of an inferiority complex, after which the Hajj was altered and the religion of Ibrahim eroded.

books.context: The main and most widely sold reference. Translated and published in Malaysia by Yadim. The ustaz does not limit himself to this book. He also mentions the author's view that Hajar was descended from a Pharaoh.

The ustaz consulted more than 40 books in several languages, including books newly bought at a bookshop in Bangi, among them a book written 300 years ago by a Chinese scholar about the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Source of the long hadith of Ibn Abbas RA on Hajar, Ismail, sa'i and Zamzam.
The ustaz cites Shaykh Quraish's explanation of 'accept our repentance': inspire our souls with awareness of our wrongs, regret and resolve not to repeat them.
Stories of the prophets including Ibrahim, Hajar and Ismail and the building of the Kaaba.
An explanation of the supplications of Prophet Ibrahim AS and the building of the Kaaba.

people.context: The ustaz mentions his view that, based on historical analysis, Hajar was the daughter of a Pharaoh.

people.role: Prophet, Khalilullah, father of the prophets
people.context: Father of the exploration of Mecca. Tested often, migrated often, tender-hearted, and his prayer was answered in the person of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Went with Ibrahim to Egypt and was almost taken by the Pharaoh, who seized beautiful women. The ustaz mentions signs of jealousy toward Hajar, but that was not why Hajar was left in Mecca.
At that time only three people accepted Islam after leaving their original land: Ibrahim, Sarah and Prophet Lut.

people.role: Wife of Prophet Ibrahim, mother of Ismail
people.context: A gift from the Pharaoh to Ibrahim. Showed trust in Allah, effort and courage in the valley of Mecca, and her effort was immortalised as sa'i.
Narrator of the long hadith in Sahih Bukhari about Hajar and Ismail.

people.role: Prophet, son of Ibrahim and Hajar
people.context: The answer to Ibrahim's prayer ('that has been heard'). Raised among the Arab Jurhum and became an Arabised Arab, then built the Kaaba with his father.

people.role: A tribe from Yemen who settled in Mecca
people.context: Came asking to settle with Hajar, later ruled Mecca, but became arrogant and were finally driven out by Khuza'ah.
Mentioned in the khalil hadith: if the Prophet ﷺ could take a khalil, he would choose Abu Bakr.
Cited on the meaning of repentance in Ibrahim's prayer: awareness of wrong, regret and resolve not to repeat.
An example of ihsan: when she gave charity she made it excellent, sometimes even putting perfume on it.
Granted at the age of 100. All prophets after him until the end of time, except Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, came from his descendants.

people.role: Ancestor of the Prophet ﷺ from the line of Ismail
people.context: A son of Prophet Ismail who became an ancestor of the Prophet ﷺ, and the last of his descendants to be driven from Mecca.

people.role: The tribe that took control of Mecca, and its chief
people.context: Defeated Jurhum. Amr ibn Luhayy brought the idol Hubal home from Rome and placed it before the Kaaba, then altered the Hajj.

lessons.title: Value health and free time before they are taken away
lessons.body: The two blessings people forget most are good health and free time. We often value them only when they diminish.

lessons.title: The story of Prophet Ibrahim is the core of our story
lessons.body: Every day in prayer we send blessings on Prophet Ibrahim, and the Prophet ﷺ described himself as resembling his father Ibrahim in appearance and struggle.

lessons.title: Human life is too precious to sacrifice to a god
lessons.body: Sacrificing a child was a practice of the time to ask for rain or protection. Allah corrected it by substituting a ram, teaching that human life is far more valuable.

lessons.title: Obey Allah's command even when it hurts
lessons.body: Prophet Ibrahim left his son and wife in a place that without Allah's help would certainly mean death, without looking back. The ustaz invites us to appreciate how painful that was for him.

lessons.title: True tawakkul: maximum effort, the rest to Allah
lessons.body: Hajar was sure Allah would not abandon them, yet she still strove up Safa and Marwah. Tawakkul comes from 'wakil', meaning to leave the matter to Allah after doing all one can.

lessons.title: Quiet effort is not wasted with Allah
lessons.body: Nobody saw Hajar, but Allah made it a rite that billions repeat. Even the reward in this world is that great.

lessons.title: Good change demands sacrifice and courage
lessons.body: Many know what they must stop but are unwilling to lose their comfort. Sometimes Allah forces the change as an answer to our prayer to be closer to Him.

lessons.title: Leave the haram, trust that Allah gives a way out
lessons.body: A forbidden source of income is not our 'rice pot'. Leaving it takes courage, and Allah promises a way out and provision from unexpected places for those who are mindful of Him and rely on Him.

lessons.title: A calamity that brings you closer to Allah is good
lessons.body: Train yourself to say istirja' and ask for reward and something better in return. A calamity that makes us farther from Allah, by accusing destiny of being unjust or comparing ourselves, is a trap of the devil.

lessons.title: Don't be trapped in the past
lessons.body: The devil pulls the child of Adam from behind by trapping him in the past. Hajar chose to face change with courage.

lessons.title: Be sincere and humble even after a great deed
lessons.body: After building the Kaaba, Ibrahim and Ismail prayed 'accept from us'. The ustaz warns us not to feel like God's representatives, as Iblis did.

lessons.title: The greatest fault is not realising you are at fault
lessons.body: Before pointing at others, analyse yourself first. Iblis justified his wrong and blamed others, and that mentality ruins relations between people.

lessons.title: Do everything with ihsan
lessons.body: Do something as well as possible even if it is small. Aisha RA made her charity excellent, instead of giving what she did not want.

lessons.title: Think long-term and put children's Hereafter first
lessons.body: Ibrahim's prayer for his descendants put prayer and faith first. The ustaz warns us not to teach children, without realising it, that prayer is second and exams come first.

lessons.title: Don't be colonised in mind or feel inferior to outsiders
lessons.body: Amr ibn Luhayy brought idols from Rome because he admired their progress. The ustaz links it to our tendency to assume outsiders are more expert.

glossary.meaning: The blessing recited in the final tashahhud. The ustaz calls it the best and highest-ranked blessing.
A statement with two meanings, where what the hearer takes differs from what is meant. The ustaz gives the example of Ibrahim calling Sarah his 'sister' (in faith).
Walking back and forth seven times between Safa and Marwah in Hajj and Umrah, commemorating Hajar's search for water.
'Arabised' Arabs: not originally Arab but who became Arab through language and culture. Prophet Ismail AS and his descendants fall in this category.
The Empty Quarter, an empty region of the Arabian Peninsula still unexplored, which the ustaz links to the place of punishment that wiped out the traces of the civilisations of Ad and Thamud.
A weak hadith. The ustaz explains that weak does not mean fabricated, and uses a grade from A to F (fabricated) as an analogy.
From 'wakil': leaving the matter to Allah after doing everything one can.
The closest friend of Allah. Only Prophet Ibrahim AS and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ hold this title.
The rites and practices of Hajj. Ibrahim prayed to be taught the manasik, and Ismail taught them to his children.
The first idol brought to Mecca by Amr ibn Luhayy and placed before the Kaaba. The ustaz is unsure about the authenticity of the depictions recorded by historians.

dalil.context: The Prophet ﷺ answers the companions' question about his beginnings. The ustaz quotes only the first part, and says many hadith scholars graded this hadith sound, which is why the sirah begins with Prophet Ibrahim. The full text is shown here.
dalil.translation: The companions said to him: "Tell us about yourself." He said: "Yes. I am the supplication of my father Ibrahim and the glad tidings brought by Isa, peace be upon them both. My mother saw, when she was carrying me, that a light came out of her that lit up the palaces of Sham. I was nursed among the Banu Sa'd ibn Bakr. While I was with the lambs, two men in white came to me with a golden basin full of snow. They laid me down, split open my belly, took out my heart and split it, took a black clot out of it and threw it away. Then they washed my heart and my belly with that snow and put them back as they were. One said to his companion: 'Weigh him against ten of his community.' They weighed me against ten and I outweighed them. Then: 'Weigh him against a hundred of his community.' I outweighed them. Then: 'Weigh him against a thousand of his community.' I outweighed them. Then he said: 'Leave him. If you weighed him against his whole community, he would outweigh them.'"

dalil.context: The ustaz links the Ibrahimic blessing in the tashahhud to Prophet Ibrahim's greeting to us.
dalil.translation: Prophet Ibrahim was leaning against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur and welcomed 'welcome, my righteous son'. The Prophet ﷺ said I most resemble my father Ibrahim, and Ibrahim sent greetings to his community.

dalil.context: Used to reject the story that Hajar was merely a slave. The ustaz mentions Al-Mubarakfuri's view that Hajar was the daughter of a Pharaoh of high standing.
dalil.translation: None of the Prophet's ﷺ ancestors or forefathers was born of fornication.

dalil.context: A long hadith. The ustaz reads the key parts, and the Prophet ﷺ describes sa'i as a continuation of Hajar's act.
dalil.translation: Hajar and Ismail were left in Mecca with a few dates and water. Hajar asked whether Allah had commanded it, and Ibrahim said yes, and Hajar said Allah will not let them be lost. Hajar went back and forth between Safa and Marwah seven times before Zamzam gushed forth.

dalil.context: Prophet Ibrahim's prayer when leaving his descendants in a valley with no vegetation: that they establish prayer, that people's hearts incline to them, and that they be provided with fruits so they might be grateful. The surah and verse number are not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Our Lord, I have established some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley, close to Your Sacred House, Lord, so that they may keep up the prayer. Make people’s hearts turn to them, and provide them with produce, so that they may be thankful.

dalil.context: A part of the same hadith of Ibn Abbas.
dalil.translation: May Allah have mercy on the mother of Ismail. Had she not held back that water, Zamzam would have become a flowing spring.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this hadith is weak (weak, not fabricated), so it should not be relied on.
dalil.translation: Prophet Ibrahim rode the Buraq from Palestine to visit Ismail, like a father raising his child from afar.

dalil.context: Two requests: reward for the calamity and something better in return. The ustaz stresses that a calamity that brings us closer to Allah is good.
dalil.translation: Indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return. O Allah, reward me in my calamity and replace it with something better.

dalil.context: The words of istirja' that the Prophet ﷺ taught for when calamity strikes. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: those who say, when afflicted with a calamity, ‘We belong to God and to Him we shall return.’

dalil.context: Allah gives a way out to those who are mindful of Him. The surah and verse number are not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: When they have completed their appointed term, either keep them honourably, or part with them honourably. Call two just witnesses from your people and establish witness for the sake of God. Anyone who believes in God and the Last Day should heed this: God will find a way out for those who are mindful of Him,

dalil.context: Allah gives provision from where they do not expect, and whoever relies on Him, He is sufficient for him. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: and will provide for them from an unexpected source; God will be enough for those who put their trust in Him. God achieves His purpose; God has set a due measure for everything.

dalil.context: The wording of the supplication is not mentioned in the lecture.
dalil.translation: Whoever recites this supplication seven times in the morning and evening, Allah will suffice him in his needs of this world and the next.

dalil.context: Prophet Ibrahim and Prophet Ismail raised the foundations of the Kaaba, then prayed 'accept from us'. Scholars hold that its foundations already existed and were rebuilt.
dalil.translation: As Abraham and Ishmael built up the foundations of the House [they prayed], ‘Our Lord, accept [this] from us. You are the All Hearing, the All Knowing.

dalil.context: Khalil is the closest friend, a title held only by Prophet Ibrahim and Prophet Muhammad.
dalil.translation: If I could take a khalil, I would take Abu Bakr. But Allah has taken me as a khalil.

dalil.context: The prayer to be made Muslims, for descendants to be a Muslim community, to be taught the Hajj rites and for repentance to be accepted.
dalil.translation: Our Lord, make us devoted to You; make our descendants into a community devoted to You. Show us how to worship and accept our repentance, for You are the Ever Relenting, the Most Merciful.

dalil.context: The prayer that Allah send a messenger from their descendants who recites the verses, teaches the Book and wisdom, and purifies them.
dalil.translation: Our Lord, make a messenger of their own rise up from among them, to recite Your revelations to them, teach them the Scripture and wisdom, and purify them: You are the Mighty, the Wise.’

dalil.context: Mentioned in the context of the beginning of idols in Mecca.
dalil.translation: The Prophet ﷺ saw Amr ibn Luhayy dragging his intestines in the Fire, because he was the first to change the religion of Ibrahim into shirk.

sirah.era: Background before the Prophet's ﷺ birth: from Prophet Ibrahim AS to the first idol at the Kaaba
sirah.summary: The ustaz paints the place and time background of the Prophet's ﷺ sirah. Ibrahim AS explored Mecca, the Kaaba was built, and over about 2,000 years the religion of Ibrahim eroded until an idol was set beside the Kaaba.

events.label: Time of Ibrahim
events.title: Prophet Ibrahim, Sarah and the gift of Hajar
events.desc: After the journey to Egypt, Ibrahim also married Hajar and was granted Ismail.

events.label: In Mecca
events.title: Hajar and Ismail left in a lifeless valley
events.desc: By Allah's command. Hajar was sure Allah would not abandon them.

events.label: Zamzam
events.title: Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, then Zamzam gushed forth
events.desc: Hajar strove seven times, then water gushed. It became part of the rites of Hajj and Umrah.

events.label: New residents
events.title: The Arab Jurhum settle and Ismail is Arabised
events.desc: Jurhum asked to settle and Hajar insisted the water was hers. Ismail grew up as an Arabised Arab.

events.label: Kaaba
events.title: Ibrahim and Ismail build the Kaaba
events.desc: After Hajar died. The structure was raised again from existing foundations, accompanied by the supplications of Al-Baqarah 127 to 129.

events.label: Decline
events.title: Jurhum driven out by Khuza'ah, Zamzam buried
events.desc: Before this there were no idols before the Kaaba. Jurhum buried the well of Zamzam before they fell.

events.label: First idol
events.title: Amr ibn Luhayy brings Hubal to Mecca
events.desc: Out of an inferiority complex on seeing advanced Rome, after which the Hajj was altered and the religion of Ibrahim was hardly practised.

events.label: Span
events.title: About 2,000 years from Ismail to the Prophet ﷺ
events.desc: Great change happened slowly, with about 21 generations between Adnan and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
